description:
File: crate-jmap-chat-server/src/backend.rs:469-477

  fn apply_space_metadata_patch(
      &self,
      caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
      account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
      space_id: &jmap_types::Id,
      patch_map: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value>,
  ) -> impl ...;

serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> appears verbatim in the
trait method signature, locking jmap-chat-server's public API to
serde_json's major version. If serde_json cuts 2.0 with any
reshape of Map or Value (the type-pair is unusually stable, but
not contractually guaranteed), every ChatBackend implementor
breaks.

Compare with apply_space_patch (backend.rs:399-405) which takes
Vec<SpacePatchOp> — a workspace-owned type. The two trait methods
do similar work but use different shapes for the patch payload.
That asymmetry is itself a contract gap; the kit could pick one.

Aggravating factors:

1. The doc says 'The handler builds patch_map by walking the
   wire patch and keeping only the keys in METADATA_FIELDS.'
   That set is tiny — name, description, iconBlobId, isPublic,
   isPubliclyPreviewable. A typed struct (5 Option fields) would
   capture it precisely AND give consumers compile-time evidence
   of what they need to handle.

2. With serde_json::Map, a consumer's apply_space_metadata_patch
   impl has to:
   - Look up keys by string (no compile-time spelling check).
   - serde_json::from_value each cell individually.
   - Handle unrecognized keys defensively (the handler is
     supposed to strip them, but a consumer calling this method
     directly has no such guarantee).
   Every consumer writes the same boilerplate.

Fix options:

A. Define a workspace-owned typed shape:
     #[non_exhaustive]
     pub struct SpaceMetadataPatch {
         pub name: Option<Clearable<String>>,
         pub description: Option<Clearable<String>>,
         pub icon_blob_id: Option<Clearable<Id>>,
         pub is_public: Option<bool>,
         pub is_publicly_previewable: Option<bool>,
     }

   Clearable from jmap-chat-types preserves the 'absent vs null
   vs set' three-way distinction. The handler decodes the wire
   patch into this struct; the backend gets a typed view.

B. Reuse jmap_chat_types::space_set::SpaceMetadataPatch if one
   exists (a quick glance suggests space-set.rs is structural-
   ops focused, but worth checking before designing a new type).

Either option drops the serde_json type from the trait surface.
Workspace AGENTS.md 'Implementation leakage' is explicit on this:
'Trait bounds on public methods that constrain callers to specific
upstream implementations.'
title: API contract: apply_space_metadata_patch leaks serde_json::Map into trait signature
